en: The Ritual for the Practice and Contemplation of the Tathāgata Cintāmaṇicakra-padmagarbha-hṛdaya, as Spoken by the Buddha;
Translated during the Song Dynasty by the State Preceptor of the Great Qidan (Liao) Empire, [Hui]zhao, of Magadha in Central India.
At that time, the Bhagavān, together with the great bodhisattvas,
was on the summit of Mount Sumeru, expounding for the sake of all sentient beings the secret method of practice of the Cintāmaṇicakra.
The Buddha said: This Lotus Maṇi Cintāmaṇicakra Vajrarāja Tathāgata possesses immeasurable and boundless,
great, inconceivable practices, and the most supreme power of majestic virtue.
Having subdued all Māras, so that no evil may enter,
you should listen well: I shall now extensively analyze this for those who seek the Dharma in the future final age.
First, pay homage to the ācārya; receive the three types of empowerment and first listen to and receive the various teachings.
Once the faculties and nature have been matured, inform the ācārya, and only then shall the transmission be bestowed in due order.
The Heart Dharma of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel: Once the disciple has completed receiving the dharma, they should give rise to a heart of sincere devotion.
With incense, flowers, lamps, unguents, food, drink, and so forth, they should first make offerings to all the Buddhas.
Having made offerings in accordance with the Dharma, one holds the perception of jewels within the mouth and petitions all Buddhas, saying:
"May I swiftly attain accomplishment in this dharma-gate. Thereupon, one binds the seal of the maṇḍala wheel.
First, the two hands perform a circular dance; then, crossing behind the back ten times and rotating until reaching the crown, they are released.
Having bound this mudrā, one gains universal access to all maṇḍalas and is able to enter all mantras.
Next, bind the Samaya seal: join the two hands in the Lotus Secret Seal;
bend the thumbs and ring fingers like a lotus in its initial opening. This is named the Cintāmaṇicakra.
The Lotus Samādhi Seal. The Samādhi Mantra is as follows:
Having bound the previous samaya seal, recite this mantra at the crown of one’s own head, as well as in the five directions and the four intermediate corners.
Empower the nine locations; next, empower the six sense organs and the two knees.
Form the mudrā of dispersal at the forehead, then form the mudrā of invocation with both hands in vajra-fists.
The *śīla* (precept) and *vīrya* (effort) fingers extend forward; the back hands interlace and hook together.
The *dhyāna* (meditation) and *prajñā* (wisdom) fingers press down the *kṣānti* (patience) and *praṇidhāna* (vow) fingers.
With the two *vīrya* fingers, one moves toward and away from the upper direction to invite the assembly of all holy ones.
Having performed the circumambulatory dance and joined the two hands like a lotus,
one should recite this mantra. Before beginning the ritual procedure,
one should first enter the river and take [water] from before one's body.
Together with the earth from the right side,
place it in the left hand and form the shape of one's own body; with the hand,
circumambulate one's own body three times in front of the face, and gaze upon it with the eyes.
Visualizing one's own actions of body, speech, and mind, as well as the six defilements,
enter into that earthen image; one should then go to a secluded place,
perform the ritual, and cast it away using one's own two hands.
In a secluded place, purify [the hands] with water nine times;
then, using cleansing powder (sādhana), wash both hands thoroughly.
With the palms cupped together, imagine bathing the Buddha.
And for the assembly of Bodhisattvas, as well as for the Dharma-ācārya, one performs three offerings using [the water]. With both hands, scoop up water twice;
then, from between the right hand’s thumb and forefinger, pour the water down into the palm.
When bathing one's parents, one should bathe them nine times;
one should thoroughly wash one’s own body as well. Finally, taking water with the right hand, one should pour it over their heads while visualizing one’s own body [as being thus purified].
Both internally and externally completely pure, having finished bathing as described above,
one should go to the entrance of the maṇḍala. Outside the maṇḍala gate,
one should first wash the feet with water, and next, one should wash both hands.
The right hand is turned upward like a vessel:
bend the *tarjanī* (forefinger) of the right hand at the joint and place it upon the palm.
Take water and pour it into the palm, inhaling the water from within the palm three times, while visualizing the purification of the three karmas.
Next, use purified water; sprinkle it toward the inside of the mandala gate to signify the rite of purifying the altar.
One should recite the root mantra to empower the purified water. The mantra for purified water is as follows:
Having recited this mantra, one should contemplate the purity of both the internal and external;
next, one should invite all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions,
and subsequently, with focused attention, one should mentally invoke them universally from within the heart-mind.
Prostrate with the five limbs touching the ground, visualize paying homage to the assembly of all the holy ones.
Having recited this invocation, visualize within yourself that all matters have been accomplished;
then one should again perform the ritual act by sprinkling water upon the maṇḍala.
In the four directions and the four intermediate corners,
one should sprinkle the substances used within the mandala to purify them. Next,
the practitioner should visualize a radiant jewel pavilion, and further visualize a golden lotus flower.
Visualize the flowers as being vast and expansive, with all four sides perfectly level and upright.
The mantra for visualizing the foundation of the jeweled pavilion is as follows:
The practitioner should next visualize the foundation of the multi-storied pavilion on its four sides.
Next, one should again visualize the ocean, its waters transforming into milk.
Then, within that ocean of milk, one should visualize four corners of ground established upon golden lotuses, and upon these, Mount Sumeru is placed.
Make the octagon square and regular; visualize above it a jeweled pavilion adorned with various kinds of jewels. The mantra of Acala is as follows:
Next, visualize the jeweled pavilion, its tiers all exquisitely decorated.
Four gates are established on the four sides,
adorned with various necklaces and canopies of the seven treasures; within the multi-storied pavilions,
windows are further constructed using mani-jewels.
Next, use various precious jewels strung together and suspended all around;
as with the aforementioned types of jewels, they all emit manifold rays of light,
making offerings everywhere to the Tathāgatas of the ten directions.
And for the assembly of Bodhisattvas, the mantra for making offerings is as follows:
Having made offerings by means of mental visualization,
one should first spread gold within the precious pavilion and visualize a lion throne above it.
Above, there is a precious lotus flower; its stem, leaves, filaments, and anthers are adorned with petals of six colors.
Within these petals, one should employ hundreds of thousands of precious jewels, interspersed and arrayed as ornaments.

Within it is the Lion Mandala; externally, one should visualize hundreds of thousands of varieties of lotus lion mandalas surrounding it in a complete and perfect array. The Lotus Mantra is as follows:
Reciting the mantra while performing the visualization, once the ritual arrangement has been completed according to the dharma,
one should use a precious vessel filled with the seven jewels,
the five grains, incense, flowers, and so forth, and visualize it before the assembly of holy beings.
With my right foot extended in prostration, I offer this homage to Sukhāvatī;
with a focused mind, I invoke the assembly of noble ones and the retinue of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
With a sincere heart, we universally invite you to descend into the center of the altar.
Before the assembly of holy ones, we shall arrange various incenses,
flowers, white whisks, banners, pennants, canopies, musical instruments, and lamps.
First, welcome the assembly of holy ones; with compassion, they descend to attend.

Next, form the seal of offering: interlace the two hands at the wrists, extend the *tarjanī* and *sūci* fingers side by side, and place the *kṣānti*, *praṇidhi*, *vīrya*, and *jñāna* fingers in sequence.
Slightly curved like a lotus petal; next, bind the mudrā of invitation with the two fingers of dhyāna and prajñā slightly curved.
Interlace the fingers of the two hands in the *kṣepa* (square) position with the backs turned toward each other and hook them together;
press the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers upon the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhāna* fingers.
The Hook for Advancing Power to Come and Go. The mantra for invitation is as follows:
Having completed the welcoming invitation as above, invite the assembly of noble ones to take their seats.
Next, form the seal for offering the seats: bend the thumbs and ring fingers of both hands.
The precepts are slightly relaxed for the sake of opening [the path]; the remaining pāramitās are likewise opened and dispersed.
Next, visualize washing the Buddha’s feet; the mantra for washing the feet says:
"May all the holy assemblies of the ten directions be visualized as having their feet washed."
All offerings whatsoever are presented with equanimity;
next, one binds the seal of universal offering, which is perfectly complete in its equality.
The right wing [of the hand] consists of the fingers of restraint, patience, and diligence, all three held straight and upright.
*Qu-cian-du-ya-tan*: One should place this on the left side of the chest with the palm facing upward to rest upon the heart.
Visualize holding objects of offering and, directing the mind, universally offer them to all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions.
The mantra for making offerings to all the assemblies of noble ones is as follows:
Form the wish-fulfilling jewel mudrā by interlocking the backs of the two vajra fists with the thumbs and ring fingers; visualize it in the form of a precious gem.
Advancing with force, pull it open. The Heart Jewel Mantra of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel is as follows.
Next, using the Lotus Heart Jewel Seal of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel:
Empower the five locations— namely the crown of the head,
the forehead, the throat, the heart, and the two shoulders. While performing the mudrās for empowerment,
one should visualize these five locations as the seats where all the noble assemblies reside.
Recite the root mantra three times. Next, with the Heart Jewel Mudrā, establish the boundary at the four cardinal directions and the four intermediate corners, as well as above and below;
internally visualize that the boundary is thus established. The mantra for the boundary is as follows:
Form the mudrās and recite the mantras to establish the inner and outer boundary;
next, recite the armor mantra to protect one’s own body.
Having performed the empowerment as described above, form the vajrakīla mudrā.
Interlace the two palms within; extend the forefingers straight upward and join the thumbs together.
One should first employ this mudrā to empower and protect the body, while reciting the mantra of the previously mentioned armor.
Having performed the empowerment to protect the body,
one should employ the mudrā while visualizing it as being driven into the ground like a stake. Using the mudrā,
turn to the right while visualizing the binding of the mandala boundary, imagining it to be like a vajra city.
Having made both the internal and external firm and having performed the visualization according to the Dharma,
the practitioner should with sincere devotion present the five kinds of offerings to the assembly of noble ones, praying that they will compassionately accept them.
First, bind the ointment mudrā: rotate the two hands first in a dance-like motion;

interlace the thumbs and little fingers; extend the remaining eight fingers straight upward and outward as if applying ointment, while visualizing that you are anointing the feet of the assembly of noble ones.
Wipe and rub the Buddha’s chest. The mantra for applying scented paste is as follows:
Next, form the Flower-scattering Mudrā. Join the two hands with the tips touching, in the shape of cupping an object.
Visualize flowers being placed upon the Buddha’s crown.
Next, bind the incense mudrā: with both hands facing upward, interlace the fingers and extend the ring fingers straight up. The mantra for burning incense is as follows.
Next, bind the lamp mudrā: with both hands facing upward, interlace the fingers.

The *kṣānti* and *vara* fingers are joined at their tips; the *dhyāna* and *jñāna* fingers should be placed alongside the two *kṣānti* and *vara* fingers. The mantra for the Lamp of Wisdom is as follows.
Next, form the seal of food and drink: the two hands are positioned in the *śīla* mudrā.
The second [finger] has its head aligned; the remaining fingers are slightly curved, like the posture of holding rice in one's hands. The Buddha’s food mantra is as follows:
Having made such offerings, the practitioner should apply their mind with sincere devotion.
Internally, one should visualize making universal offerings to the assembly of all the holy ones of the ten directions.
Having performed the mantra-offering, one should visualize paying homage to the eight bodies— namely,
those of the five directions above the crown of the head, as well as those at the forehead, mouth, and heart.
One should sincerely direct one's thoughts toward making prostrations. The mantra for prostrating to the Buddha says:

"Having paid homage to the assembly of noble ones, one should relinquish the perception of one's own body and conceive of it as a precious pavilion; one should then [visualize] within the heart-mind..."

Visualize the Lotus-Vajra; above it, upon a sun and moon mandala, visualize the essence of True Suchness (Tathatā), remaining motionless and profoundly tranquil within the moon mandala. Next, upon that moon mandala...
Furthermore, visualize the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel (Cintāmaṇicakra) and the Tathāgata Padmarāja seated there with dignified composure.
Direct your visualization with single-minded focus and do not allow the mind to become distracted;
you should then address the assembly of noble ones.
I pray that you will deign to extend your heart of great compassion and show me the practice of skillful means.
May the supreme deeds I perform bestow [benefit] upon all sentient beings, causing them all to ascend to perfect enlightenment. Having thus made this declaration to the assembly of noble ones:
Furthermore, within the mind of the Wheel-Turning King, one visualizes a moon disc; upon the moon,
one visualizes the syllable HŪṂ, the size of a barley grain,
possessing pervasive radiance that extends throughout the realms of the ten directions.
Having recited this syllable HŪṂ, one should next visualize that the syllable HŪṂ transforms into light of six colors; within this light,
it changes into six bodhisattvas, each holding offering substances.
Pervading the three thousandfold world system, he universally makes offerings to all the Buddhas,
the Bhagavāns of the three times. Having made these offerings through emanated light,
he again withdraws it into the syllable *HŪṂ*, which returns to the moon disc within his heart.
Above the syllable HŪṂ, there again appears a moon disc maṇḍala with a lotus upon which lies a vajra;
as before, the sun and moon discs and the lion maṇḍala are adorned in exactly the same manner, without any difference.
Above, one should visualize the Great Lotus Tathāgata,
whose appearance is golden in color; his right hand should hold a wish-fulfilling maṇi jewel, and his left hand should grasp [a lotus].
Upon a great golden lotus, his body is draped in exquisite garments;
with *maṇi* jewels strung together, he wears a necklace.
Next, one should form the *Cintāmaṇicakra* (Wish-Fulfilling Wheel) *maṇi* root mudrā.
First, join the two palms together; extend the thumbs and ring fingers like a jewel while bending the index fingers like a needle.
The middle fingers, wisdom-fingers, and little fingers should be held straight and spread apart, with the thumbs and wisdom-fingers both slightly curved.
Visualize [the deity] like a blossoming lotus and recite the root mantra.
Next, again form the heart mudrā: join the two hands at the tips of the six fingers.
Place each [finger] within the gaps of the others; extend the force of the fingers twice and bend the tips so they are half an inch apart.
Open the *cena* (middle) and *jñāna* (little) fingers, standing upright like a lotus first opening. One should then visualize this mudrā.
Place it within the mind. The heart-mantra is as follows:
form the seal of the heart-within-the-heart. With both hands, join the tips of the thumbs and the ring fingers so that their faces touch; extend the remaining eight fingers straight upward.
With the seal lowered and directed downward, visualize it upon the heart-seal;
thus, having established the mind within one's own body through the mental application of the Cintāmaṇicakra and the Heart-to-Heart Seal.
Furthermore, from within the heart of the heart, there emanates the one named Krodha,
known as the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel (Cintāmaṇicakra).
This Lotus-Heart Mantra King is pale red in appearance, with a garland of flowers for his necklace.
Adorned with various ornaments, holding a hook-staff in his right hand and a lasso in his left,
he stood to the right of the Buddha and addressed him,
saying: "World-Honored One, may the Buddha please grant me instructions."
"May you cause me to accomplish all tasks. Next, one should visualize the Buddha’s Rosary Mother to the left of the Buddha;
she is seated with her left knee drawn up in the *hukuei* (half-lotus) posture, is reddish-white in color, and wears a rosary draped around her neck.
The two hands are like those holding prayer beads; their posture is identical to the stance for recitation.
The Mother is represented as the Body-Vidyārāja, and her power is represented as Force.
Having recited this mantra of the rosary-body, one threads it through the eight consciousnesses.
Holding the rosary with both hands, one should first perform a prostration at the crown of the head;
having empowered it with the mantra, one should then visualize placing a moon-mandala upon the heart, and upon that, place the rosary.
Visualize the rosary as the Mother of the Buddhas;
the Vidyārāja and the mantra are one and the same, without distinction.
Whenever performing recitation, one should first visualize the Mother of the Rosary to the left of the Buddha.
Seated upon the lunar disc, one should inwardly extend prostrations and recite the mantra seven times. Having performed such visualization,
one should further contemplate within the mind incense, flowers, and lamps.
With a focused mind, perform the offering once more to the Tathāgata Cintāmaṇicakra and the Vidyārājñī;
then, having recited the empowerment ritual for the name of the Vidyārājñī, perform the inner offering once again.
To summon all the Buddhas and the assembly of sages,
perform prostrations and form the preceding Lotus Mudrā. Visualize the two hands as opening lotuses and supporting the assembly of sages, then return them to their original positions.
Recite this to respectfully escort the vidyās; visualize that the assembly of Buddhas and noble ones each returns to their pure lands.
Having escorted the assembly of noble ones, next perform the mudrā for releasing the boundary:
extend the two hands with the fingers of the *saṃvara* [mudrā] crossed.
As for the *vajra-vīrya* fingers, they are all interlaced and hooked;
the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers press down upon the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhāna* fingers.
One flicks the two *vīrya* fingers as if opening the gate of a mandala; circling three times to the left completes the release.
The vajra-kīla employed, as well as the boundary lines, are all withdrawn by means of the mudrā.
The mantra for releasing the boundary is recited while performing the mudrā;
having thus released the boundaries both inside and out—
At the time of offering, one should further visualize the assembly of noble beings descending with nectar water,
which washes away the karmic obscurations of one's own body and eliminates them,
so that both internally and externally all is purified.
The Buddha told the practitioner: "Diligently cultivate this Dharma and do not give rise to weariness. Recite and uphold it without interruption;
before long you shall achieve accomplishment, equal to that of the Buddha without distinction."
The Ritual for the Practice of the Contemplation Gate of the Tathāgata Cintāmaṇicakra-padmagarbha-hṛdaya, as Spoken by the Buddha, is hereby completed.
